title: kb_pack prints a route and what the kb has and lacks
goal: rag.py pack, pack -q and kb_pack print, on every weak or none pack and every flagged good pack (a check: line, or a question word nowhere in the kb), three lines after the coverage, check:, freshness: and none sentence lines and before the first article: `route: web` (none) or `route: split` (weak, flagged good, and a near-miss none), `kb has:` (the question's own words the best article matches) and `kb lacks:` (its informative words the best article does not match), computed without a model; a pack of several parts starts with one overall route line (web when every part routes web, else split when any part routes); a clean good pack prints what it printed before, with no route line.

notes: Operator answers: pack stays model-free, stdlib only; no new always-on tokens (the lines print only on routed packs, never in server instructions or tool descriptions); clean good unchanged. The last two checks pass now on purpose: they guard the existing check: line tests (test_kb.py asserts `check:` on the pack's second line) and the lookup eval, which the new lines must not break. Routing on a lexical verdict has the shape of CRAG's corpus-then-web fallback, but the papers' gains do not transfer as numbers (agents/hybrid-retrieval.md:108-110, DOC S-dghvtpkr, DER S-5y6g7iij, S-dghvtpkr, S-yknt2enl). Measured on HEAD over lookup_eval.csv: 170 of the 174 rows expected good pack good; 3 carry a check: line, 0 a word nowhere in the kb, 38 a known word the best article does not match; which of these count as flagged is gate `flagged`.
